claims.text: Under the 2023 Fed stress test severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 capital ratio of the 23 tested banks declined from an actual 12.4 percent at the start of the projection horizon (2022:Q4) to a projected minimum of 9.9 percent, then rose to 10.5 percent by the end of nine quarters (2025:Q1), and aggregate and individual post-stress CET1 ratios remained well above required minimums throughout the horizon.

citations.quotation:
Under the severely adverse scenario, the aggregate CET1 capital ratio is projected to decline from
12.4 percent at the start of the projection horizon to a minimum of 9.9 percent before rising to
10.5 percent at the end of nine quarters

The aggregate and individual bank post-stress
common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratios remain well above the required minimum levels
throughout the projection horizon.

counterarguments.text: The 12.4 percent starting point is an actual 2022:Q4 value, while the 9.9 percent minimum and 10.5 percent ending ratio are projections under a hypothetical scenario, not observed outcomes; results also depend on scenario assumptions and model choices. Additionally, some figures (projected 2025:Q1 and projected minimum columns, AOCI rows) were revised in the report, so earlier-published values may differ.
